subject: Hightide Labs: sudden latency and 5xx surge — routing/DNS/proxy investigation + exec sync
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@hightide.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@hightide.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T08:50:00-08:00
Subject: Production latency + 5xx spike — started ~08:30 PST

Jordan / Marissa,

We're seeing a sudden production regression across our checkout and recommendation endpoints starting ~08:30 PST. Key symptoms:
- p50 for text-generation API jumped from ~80ms to ~420ms over the last 30m
- p95 moved from 360ms -> 2.1s
- 5xx rate (502/504) spiked to ~6.7% for the last 20 minutes
- Error traces show a mix of proxy 502s and TLS handshake timeouts

This is impacting our checkout flow for the holiday promotion — conversions are dropping. I've attached latency graphs and a short collection of request ids. Can you confirm if anything changed on the routing/peering side?

Attaching: hightide_latency_graphs.pdf

Alex
Sr. SRE, Hightide Labs

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@hightide.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spike — initial triage

Doing initial network/edge triage now — posting findings.

What I ran:
- active traceroutes from our US-west inference cluster to Hightide's ingress IPs (samples attached)
- collection of proxy logs around 08:20–09:00 PST

Prelim indicators:
- Several traces show traffic hairpinning through Peer-A (VPC peering) with an extra hop where we see elevated retransmits and increased RTTs (~40–300ms variance)
- Edge proxy logs indicate a burst of backend 502s correlated with high conntrack counts on the upstream NAT at Peer-A (we saw conntrack ~80–90% of configured limit for a short window)
- DNS: no mass NXDOMAINs, but TTLs appear to be being refreshed more frequently from Hightide's side (short TTLs ~30s) which may be amplifying churn during the surge

Attachments: trace_hops.txt (sample traceroute + hop RTTs)

Immediate mitigations I'm proposing (can be done in next 20–40 min once approved):
1) Add a temporary failover route for subset of Hightide traffic to go through Peer-B (lower-latency path) — reduces hairpin and NAT pressure
2) Increase conntrack limits on Peer-A as a short-term measure (15–60m) while we shift routes
3) Coordinate with Hightide to lengthen DNS TTL to reduce resolution churn during the promotion surge

Risks: route change will cause cache flushes and a small reconnection spike; conntrack bump is low-risk but requires admin ACL change ticket. Recommend we do 1 + 2 immediately and request 3 from Hightide.

Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Priya Singh <priya@hightide.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hightide SRE Team <sre@hightide.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T09:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spike — initial triage

Thanks — confirming a few points from our side:
- We had a promotion start at 08:00 PST which resulted in a sustained ~3x baseline traffic increase across the inference endpoints.
- Our edge team rolled a DNS change at 07:55 (short TTL to enable rapid rollback for the promo) — TTL was set to 30s. We can revert to 300s if that helps; will require coordination with our CDN team (~5–10m).
- We see the same NAT/conntrack lift on Peer-A from our telemetry. We can approve a short-term TTL increase and will open a ticket to extend the TTL.

We also have an internal firewall ACL that blocks some CIDR ranges by default when traffic exceeds thresholds — I can temporarily relax that rule for Redwood's inference IP ranges if you can provide the exact CIDRs to whitelist.

Priya Singh
Head of Production Engineering, Hightide Labs
priya@hightide.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-19T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Hightide incident — exec summary + ask

Lauren — quick executive summary and asks (sharing for approval / escalation):

Summary (tl;dr):
- Customer: Hightide Labs experiencing p95 latency spikes and ~6–7% 5xx due to a converging set of issues: promotion-driven traffic surge, short DNS TTLs causing resolution churn, and an overloaded NAT/conntrack state on Peer-A that is increasing retransmits and proxy 502s.
- Impact: Major checkout flow degradation during a revenue-critical promo window. Customer conversion impacted. Exec attention requested.

Immediate recommended actions (need approval):
- Approve emergency route shift: divert ~30% of Hightide traffic through Peer-B for next 60 minutes while we observe (this reduces hairpinning).
- Approve admin change to increase conntrack limits on Peer-A (15–45 minutes, reversible).
- Coordinate with Hightide to increase DNS TTL to 300s (customer leads are already on board).
- Offer a goodwill credit if SLA breach confirmed for the promo period (need sign-off from finance/sales).

Requested approvals:
- Greenlight route shift + conntrack bump now so Ben can implement immediately.
- I'll run the exec sync at 11:30 PST with Hightide leadership to confirm public comms and any customer credit.

If you approve, I'll proceed and copy you on the change ticket and the post-incident summary.

Jordan Blake
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@hightide.com>, Priya Singh <priya@hightide.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T15:47:00-08:00
Subject: Exec sync scheduled & mitigation plan (11:30 PST follow-up)

All — thanks for the quick coordination. Final notes and actions before the 11:30 PST exec sync:

What we did (completed at ~09:50 PST):
- Route change: shifted 35% of Hightide traffic to Peer-B (temporary, measured rollout) — observed p95 drop from 2.1s -> 520ms within 5 minutes
- Conntrack bumped by +30% on Peer-A; NAT pressure dropped and 502s decreased by ~70% in the affected window
- Hightide reverted TTL to 300s at 09:42 PST which reduced resolution churn

Outstanding items / next steps:
- Change ticket created for firewall ACL relaxation (Hightide is preparing CIDR list).
- Post-incident: we'll run a full traffic-path root cause analysis and share a remediation plan (BGP routing preference adjustments, peer capacity review, and DNS operational guidance).
- Jordan to own customer comms and potential goodwill credit proposal with Sales/Finance

Attachments: firewall_acl_changes.xlsx (change request for Peer-A conntrack + ACLs)
Links: https://docs.redwood.com/incident/HIGHTIDE-67 (live incident timeline)

Call: Exec sync 11:30 PST / 14:30 EST — dial-in on video bridge +95-183 (details on the calendar invite).

Thanks everyone — will send a short exec brief after the call.

Jordan Blake
